title: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

sense.text:
“And the Horites in their mount Seir.” The Horites were a group of Hamites, Canaanites, who lived in that land. Hamites were often named after their forefather or after the region they lived in.

This is before Esau was born, before Esau and Jacob were in existence. Later in history the so-called white man, Edom, sat in Seir, but Mount Seir belonged to the Horites first. Hold on to that, because it plays an important role in understanding who Edom is and how he took that land.

Isaac, the son of Abraham, took Rebekah to wife, and she was barren; she could not bring forth children. So Isaac prayed for her: “Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren: and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.” The Lord heard his prayer and she finally conceived.

“The children struggled together within her”: children, more than one child in her womb, and already fighting. She said, “If it be so, why am I thus?” If this is a blessing from the Lord, why am I in such pain with these children fighting in my womb? So “she went to enquire of the Lord.”

The Lord revealed that she had twins and that they were two different nations: “Two nations are in thy womb.” Two nations, two ethnicities, two nationalities. Those who say Esau was black too are wrong.

“Two manner of people”: they would look different and behave differently. They were not identical. “Shall be separated from thy bowels”: they would not be together. Some twins are inseparable; these twins would never get along, never be together in harmony and peace.

“The one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.” That does not sound equal. Two manner of people, one stronger than the other, one serving the other, and Rebekah was told it before they were born.

“The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment.” He was red all over and hairy all over. Remember that, because it plays a very important role. Jacob was not red and hairy, so they could not have been identical: they were fraternal twins, two manner of people.

There is no such thing as white people; that is a self-designated name Europeans gave themselves to say how pure and holy they were, and their actions from then until now show otherwise. The anatomy books say it plainly: the pink to red color of Caucasian skin is caused by hemoglobin, the red pigment of the blood, which shows more easily through the skin because Caucasian skin has relatively little melanin. Slap them, they get red; they cry, get angry, laugh, they get red; they are born very red. Their blood shows through their skin.

“And they called his name Esau”: wasted away, because he lacked the melanin that everyone else on the earth had. His skin was so see-through you could see his blood through it.

“After that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau’s heel; and his name was called Jacob.” Jacob is not described, because he was normal; he looked like his parents. The one who came out red and hairy was the strange child.

Jacob grabbed Esau’s heel because the fight in the womb carried on outside the womb. It was war from beginning to end; there would be moments of peace, but they never mixed, like oil and water. Isaac prayed for them at forty and got them at threescore, sixty years old.

“Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field.” He matches the blood he sheds: always running around hunting animals to extinction, hunting people, hunting resources. It is his nature. Name a black nation that killed off an entire race and took its identity, or dropped a nuclear bomb on somebody. None. They are not like us and we are not like them: two manner of people.

“Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents”: a homebody, content in the tent while Esau ran in the field.

“Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison”: Esau was the hunter, the tough one bringing home the best meat, so Isaac had a favorite. “But Rebekah loved Jacob”, because the Lord had told her that the elder shall serve the younger.

“Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint”, probably from being in that sun too long. With a lack of melanin he is not built for the sun.

“Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”, “therefore was his name called Edom.” He was already red from birth, and now he wanted the red pottage, so his name went from Esau, wasted away, to Edom, red.

“Sell me this day thy birthright.” Esau was the eldest, so by inheritance he was to receive everything: the blessings of Abraham, the kingdom. Esau said, “I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?” He was an evil man and did not respect his birthright. Jacob said, “Swear to me this day”, and “he sold his birthright unto Jacob.” The elder shall serve the younger: that was the birthright.
“Thus Esau despised his birthright.” He hated it and sold it for food: the hell with it, it was not important to him. Later on he realised it was.

“Esau my brother is a hairy man.” That did not change. He came out red and hairy all over like an hairy garment, and he grew up still red and hairy all over. The hair did not fall off as it does with some children; it stayed. That is why his name was changed to Edom.

“And I am a smooth man.” We are smooth people. Some of us have hair, but we are not furry like him.

Rebekah told Jacob to go and seek the blessing from Isaac disguised as Esau, and Jacob said if he did that his father would curse him: “I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.” But Rebekah had already seen what the Lord showed her when the twins were in her womb, that the elder shall serve the younger, and she was making certain it happened. The Lord willed it. So she said, “Upon me be thy curse, my son.”

The Muslims call Jacob a deceiver because they love Ishmael and count him the firstborn, so they try to slander Jacob. But God chose Isaac, not Ishmael, and Rebekah was only seeing to what the Lord had said.

Rebekah took the raiment of Esau and put it on Jacob, and “she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck.” Why goat fur on his hands? Because Esau was a furry man with goat-like hair out of his skin. It is very clear what this man looked like: red, with goat hair. Goat hair is stringy, thin hair, not woolly like a sheep’s. They did not put sheep’s fur on him, but the goats’ fur, so that he would appear hairy like his brother, with thin hair hanging from his hands and neck. That is the same hair so many of our own people pay for in the store today.

Isaac was blind, so he asked, “Who art thou, my son?” Jacob said, “I am Esau thy firstborn.” And Isaac asked, “How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son?” You got back fast: hunted it, cooked it, all that? Jacob answered, “Because the Lord thy God brought it to me.”

“Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son.” These were fraternal twins, so their voices were not the same; Isaac heard Jacob’s voice and had to feel him to be sure, because when he held Esau he held a furry man.

“The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.” You sound like Jacob, but you are hairy, so you have to be your brother. “He discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: so he blessed him.” Esau was extremely hairy.

“He smelled the smell of his raiment.” Having felt him, Isaac smelled him: “the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed.” Esau was a man of the field, and he smelled like outside. This had to be Esau.

“God give thee of the dew of heaven.” Dew falls everywhere, so the dew of heaven means the world: the Lord gives you the world. “And the fatness of the earth”: the best parts of the earth. “And plenty of corn and wine”: a healthy land wherever you go.

“Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee.” All nations will serve you, including your brother. That is not equality. “Be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother’s sons bow down to thee”: Jacob to rule over Esau. “Cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.”

As soon as Jacob was “scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac his father”, Esau came in from his hunting with his savoury meat. Isaac asked, “Who art thou?” and Esau said, “I am thy son, thy firstborn Esau.” “And Isaac trembled very exceedingly”, because he had just blessed someone in that house. “Yea, and he shall be blessed”: whoever was in here, I blessed him, and I am not taking it back.

Esau “cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry”: bless me, I am your oldest. Isaac said, “Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.” He came in slick.

“Is not he rightly named Jacob?” Jacob means supplanter: he took his place. “He took away my birthright”: stop there. Is that what happened? No. He sold it for food. Esau is a liar. He despised the birthright and counted on the blessing, but he lost that too, because God had other plans.

“Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants.” The elder shall serve the younger. I blessed him with everything he could need: servants, land, the earth, all the dew falls on and the fatness of the earth. What can I possibly give you?
“Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.” He was crying, and mad as hell.

“Thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” Isaac told Jacob the same thing: Esau would also have the earth in his possession, almost all of it. But there is a catch in how each of them would acquire it.

“And by thy sword shalt thou live.” That is how he would acquire it. His blessing is the blessing of warfare: the fatness of the earth and the dew of heaven taken by the sword. Firepower, nuclear fire, ballistic missiles, Tomahawk missiles, gunpowder, the knife. A warmonger. Jacob inherited those things; Esau would take them by force and steal them. That is his blessing, and that is why he is so good at it.

“And shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” Esau would be released from his brother’s power. Under David and Solomon we had him under our thumb; when Solomon fell and his sons went off, Edom was free to do as he wanted.

“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him.” He felt he was entitled to it as the eldest, but God told his mother something different. That thought has never left him: the earth belongs to me, I am the oldest, I should be the chosen people of God. That hatred went into his children, and it is still there today: enslave Jacob, destroy him as a people, make him a Gentile and make myself Israel. Israel belongs to me, America belongs to me, anywhere Jacob is belongs to me. This is war.

“And Esau said in his heart”: in his mind, not out loud. “Then will I slay my brother Jacob”: when my father dies, I will kill him.

“And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah.” How were words in his heart told to her? God told her. The Lord knew Isaac had a favorite, so he told the mother to get Jacob out of there. Esau “doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee”: he would take comfort over his dying father by killing his brother.

“Flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran; and tarry with him a few days, until thy brother’s fury turn away.” Stay there until your brother calms down. “Why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” If Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau, and she would lose them both.

Esau himself later forgot and forgave. But he told his children what Jacob did to him, and his children never forgot and never forgave.
“Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom.” His name was changed to red, Edom.

Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Aholibamah the daughter of Anah the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite. He married Hamites against his parents’ wishes, because he was rebellious, a liar, evil and a fornicator.

When his parents were angry over the Hamites, he went and married “Bashemath Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebajoth.” Still bad, still rebellious. So many of the light-skinned Arabs are Esau. Nebajoth became the father of the Nabataeans.

Adah bare Eliphaz, Bashemath bare Reuel, and Aholibamah bare Jeush, Jaalam and Korah: “these are the sons of Esau, which were born unto him in the land of Canaan.” Esau dwelt in Canaan, the land that was first his by birth but was promised to Jacob instead. When he had calmed down, he and Jacob met up and shared that land for a while.

Esau took all “his substance, which he had got in the land of Canaan.” He gained great wealth in Canaan while he lived near Jacob; both families grew there and both got very rich. Then he “went into the country from the face of his brother Jacob. For their riches were more than that they might dwell together.” They had too much cattle and too many servants to stay in one place, and the one who had to go was Esau, because that land did not belong to him.
“Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” Esau left Canaan and went to Mount Seir. Remember, the Horites dwelt in Mount Seir. What became of them? “The father of the Edomites in mount Seir.”

“These were dukes of the sons of Esau.” Dukes are high titles. Eliphaz was Esau’s firstborn, and of Eliphaz came duke Teman, duke Omar, duke Zepho, duke Kenaz, duke Korah, duke Gatam and duke Amalek: “these are the dukes that came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom.” Eliphaz birthed nearly all of these dukes.

Remember these dukes: they are all around today under different names, German, Israeli, Polish, Russian.

“These are the sons of Esau, who is Edom, and these are their dukes.” Then: “These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land.” Genesis 14:6 said the Horites dwelt in Mount Seir, so when Esau got there, the Horites were there, and their father was Seir the Horite, a Hamite.

“These are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.” Where did Esau learn about dukes? From the Horites. He got among them, took them over, and took their titles: they called themselves dukes, so we will call ourselves dukes. That is what he does: take everything.

The children of Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer and Dishan are all Horites, dukes who were there first. “These are the dukes that came of Hori, among their dukes in the land of Seir.” These were the first dukes; then Esau conquered and became dukes himself, based on these Hamites. Seir should have been Ham’s, but Seir became Edom’s instead.

“The Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime.” Horims and Horites are the same people, Hamites. “But the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them”: they intermingled with them and then conquered them out of there by the sword, “and dwelt in their stead”, and became Seir. When you read of Seir it is Edom, but it was Ham first.

“As Israel did unto the land of his possession.” We did that in Canaan, but we did not kill off all the Canaanites; they still lived there. Esau wasted no time: he killed all of them out of there.

precepts.why:
Moses says it again: the Lord did this “to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day.”

The name Horite comes from the Hebrew Hor, a cave or hole: the Horites were cave dwellers, troglodytes, living in the mountains of Seir. So Esau went in, conquered the cave dwellers, and became the cave dweller. And Caucasian means cave dweller. There are many layers to this, and they all point the same way: the white man is not Japheth; he is Esau.

sense.text: Israel asks the Lord in the spirit, “Wherein hast thou loved us?” You love us when we were constantly in captivity, over and over? The Lord answers with a question: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” “yet I loved Jacob.”

“And I hated Esau.” The Christian theologians argue that in the Hebrew hated means he preferred him less, because it sounds better. Would it sound any better to tell one son, I prefer you less than him? No. It means hate, and verse 4 proves it.

“And laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.” His mountains and his caves were laid waste for the dragons, the Arabs. Esau married into Ishmael through Nebajoth, the Nabataeans; in the time of Babylon the Nabataeans rose up and pushed much of Esau out of that land, taking it or marrying into them. Mount Seir is called Petra today, meaning rock. In that time nations were on the run and displaced until Babylon fell.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished.” When Edom was in Canaan he was rich; out in the caves of Seir he was poor, a poor cave dweller. “But we will return and build the desolate places”: we will gain power again. “Thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down.” They will build themselves up into power, and God will bring them down.

“And they shall call them, The border of wickedness.” A border is the beginning or the end of something: they are the beginning and the end of wickedness, the wicked the Bible speaks of. “And, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” The people, the whole nation. Indignation is a righteous hatred: the hate of verse 3 is the indignation of verse 4, and it is for ever. They were made to be hated. That is their lot, and that is their blessing: to be hated, and to rule by the sword.

“Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”: “an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.” This is happening now; the actions of Trump and his administration are leading up to it.

Keep this in mind: nations rising up against Edom in battle means Edom would have done what Malachi said, rebuilt the desolate places and gained power. Edom would in time gain power and no longer be impoverished.

“Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen”: a minority in the earth, not the majority. “Thou art greatly despised”: we see it now. With America helping Israel, the world is turning on Israel, and America’s own citizens are turning on America. Trump is the honest face of America that America tried to hide for centuries, and Netanyahu is his little brother, America on the other side of the earth: dropping bombs on innocent men, women and children in Gaza and on a girls’ school in Iran. The world is starting to realize this man is the devil the Bible speaks of. They exposed themselves, and now everybody hates them.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”: the boasting that everything is going great, while the gas runs out. “Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: the cave dweller. “Whose habitation is high”: the mountains. “That saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” To say such a thing you must have power. That is why verse 1 calls nations to rise up against Edom in battle: in the last days Edom would be a formidable superpower on the earth.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle.” He would have a history of dwelling in caves and would exalt himself with the eagle. The Greeks, the Romans, Spain, France, Russia, Britain and America all used the eagle; what do they all have in common? They are all Caucasians. Show a black nation that is a superpower today, exalts itself as the eagle, and dwelt in caves. It cannot be done. It fits one people: the Europeans.

“And though thou set thy nest among the stars”: space stations, satellites, a Space Force. “Thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” It is happening now. America is in the age of decadence, an empire in decline: feminism, homosexuality, sports, entertainment, the dollar dying. Make America great again means it is not great anymore, and he cannot heal it; God will not allow it. What made America great was her alliances with her European family, built on the nuke, on death and destruction, and he is burning every bridge. That is all we want: I will bring thee down, saith the Lord.

precepts.why:
When did Edom find the time to rise in power, so that the nations would say, Let us rise up against her in battle? “Israel is a scattered sheep; the lions have driven him away”: the lions are the nations. “First the king of Assyria hath devoured him”: Assyria conquered the northern kingdom. “And last this Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath broken his bones”: Babylon conquered Judah.

The kingdom split in two because of Solomon, and both halves were overthrown by Assyria and Babylon. That is when the nations began to grow in power and travel. Isaac had prophesied that Esau would break his brother’s yoke from off his neck: once Judah was conquered, Edom had no more threats, and that gave Edom time to grow and thrive, in the days of Assyria and Babylon.

sense.text: “Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it.” Mount Seir was the land of the Horites, and Edom took it over and became Seir. “Behold, O mount Seir, I am against thee, and I will stretch out mine hand against thee, and I will make thee most desolate.”

“Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred.” Esau calmed down and forgave his brother, but his descendants did not. They kept the hatred Esau had when he said he would comfort himself by killing Jacob after his father died. It passed into their blood. Perpetual means for ever, from then until now.

“And hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity”: when Babylon came against us and broke our bones, Edom was there to help. “In the time that their iniquity had an end”: fast forward, and when we got the Emancipation Proclamation they brought Jim Crow, black codes and the KKK. They extended the terror even after our so-called freedom, and they still do it now.

“I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee.” The way you shed blood, God will shed yours, and it will follow you wherever you go. “Sith thou hast not hated blood”: Esau loves blood, resembles it and sheds it.

“I will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return.” Malachi said Edom would return and build the desolate places; God says after this, no more. No more America, no more New York, no more DC, no more capitals. It is finished.

“Because thou hast said, These two nations and these two countries shall be mine.” The two nations are Judah and Ephraim, Judah and Israel, and the two countries are Judah and Samaria. It goes twofold: Israel and America too. The Americas were promised to us since the time of Moses, and Esau says whatever was given to Jacob belongs to me, because the birthright should be mine. Israel was his: no, that is my land now. America was his: my land now. Africa: mine too. Wherever Jacob runs, Edom will take it by the sword as best he can. “And we will possess it; whereas the Lord was there.”

precepts.why:
“Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.” Amalek was promised condemnation from the very beginning; there is no saving this group.

First of the nations means they were the first nation to attack us when we came out of Egypt, because of that perpetual hatred of Ezekiel 35. They held on to it. In the wilderness they attacked us from behind, where the elders, the mothers and the children were, not the front where the men were. They are cowards, with a cowardly spirit: they drop bombs and run off. They are murderous and very good at it, but very emotional; some of the dukes among them are quieter, more vicious and more in tune with that murderous nature.

“And he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel, and possessed the city of palm trees.” The king of Moab gathered Ammon and Amalek and used Amalek to conquer us and take over our land: these two countries shall be mine.

Edom always had a strong desire to take our land, going right back to the blessing he lost and the birthright he gave away. In Canaan he became very rich; when he left he became desolate, living in caves, until we fell and he gained power and prominence again after Assyria and Babylon.

Darius had vowed it: “Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.” This goes back to Ezekiel: they shed the blood of their brother in the time of his calamity. Edom had already been conquered, and helped the Babylonians overthrow Judah too.

When the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem, the Edomites were the ones who burned the temple. They destroyed the first temple, and as the Romans they destroyed the second.

Darius decreed “that all the country which they hold should be free without tribute; and that the Edomites should give over the villages of the Jews which then they held.” When Babylon overthrew us, Edom burned our temple and moved into our land, because of that hatred and because he says the land belongs to him. Then the Persians said, You do not belong here, and put them out.

It is always them trying to take our land: with Babylon, with the king of Moab, and today. This is war.

sense.text:
Ecclesiasticus was written by Jesus the son of Sirach, a wise man, around 200 to 175 BC, in the time of the Greeks, to fight against the Greek influence of his day.

“They that sit upon the mountain of Samaria”: who sat upon the mountain of Samaria in the time of the Greeks? The Greeks did, when they built their temple on Garizim. Other translations of this verse, which Bishop sent, name those that sit there as those who live in Seir, the inhabitants of Seir: Edom. Another version cuts the Edom part out on purpose. Where another version agrees with the KJV it can be used; where it does not, it is ignored. So Sirach tells you that Edom sat upon Samaria, and in that day Edom was the Greeks.

“And they that dwell among the Philistines”: the Hamites. “And that foolish people that dwell in Sichem”: the silly northern kingdom that loved the heathen, not a people.

precepts.why:
“The king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God.” The Greek king commanded Judah to leave the laws of our God and live by Greek laws and fashions. That is assimilation, integration, Hellenization: we became Greek citizens, the same as African Americans today.

“And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius”: the temple of Zeus. “And that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers.” Garizim is a mount in Samaria. So who sat upon the mount of Samaria in that day? The Greeks. That is who Sirach was speaking of: Edom sitting on Samaria as the Greeks.

“Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian, who came out of the land of Chettiim, had smitten Darius king of the Persians and Medes.” Alexander the Great’s father was Philip the Macedonian. Chettiim is Cyprus. Alexander killed Darius the Third of the Persians and Medes; the Greeks began to conquer the dark nations at this time.

This is Edom rebuilding the desolate places, as Malachi said: taking over Greece and Rome. “He reigned in his stead, the first over Greece”, and his house united Edom together and subjugated Greece and Rome. Hold on to that name, the Macedonian.

sense.text:
“King Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite.” Ahasuerus is Artaxerxes. Haman was the enemy in the book of Esther who sought to kill all the Jews out of existence.

The Agagite: Agag was the king of the Amalekites, an Edomite king. King Saul went in and slaughtered them, and Haman is of the survivors. So when Haman found that Mordecai was of the line of King Saul, he said, they tried to kill us off, kill them all. Edom and Israel go to war from generation to generation; we will never get along, from the womb to the tomb.

precepts.why:
The Apocrypha says the same: “Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.”

Haman was behind the two eunuchs who sought to kill the king and take the throne. The Greeks, Edom, infiltrated the Persian Empire, seeking to conquer it from the inside.

“For Aman, a Macedonian, the son of Amadatha, being indeed a stranger from the Persian blood.” Haman was a Macedonian. And what was Philip, Alexander the Great’s father, called in 1 Maccabees 1? The Macedonian. Haman the Agagite, the Amalekite, is Haman the Macedonian: Edom and the Macedonians are the same people. He was not Persian; he was a stranger from the Persian blood, an Edomite.

The Jewish writings say the same. They trace Haman’s line back through Agag, through the red one, to Amalek, of Eliphaz the son of Esau. In the old writings on Judaism, Idumean is used for Jewish: Herod was an Idumean, and he was Jewish, and Titus with his father, Romans, married an Idumean. The medieval chroniclers say expressly that Edom means the Roman Empire, the European powers, and that both the Jews and the Arabs regarded Esau as the Greeks and Romans. They wrote that Esau’s descendants are the sworn enemies of Jacob’s to the end of the world; that they were a small nation confined to Mount Seir while Israel ruled in Canaan; that after the twelve tribes fell to the Assyrians and Babylonians they wonderfully increased, extended their dominion toward the west, and hold dominion over all Europe; that Esau holds Jacob in captivity until the Messiah, the son of David, appears; and that the prophets’ severest judgments on Edom, especially those of Isaiah, Jeremiah and Obadiah, have not yet been fully accomplished and will be executed in the time of the Messiah. Edom is promised the most severe punishments of any nation on the earth.

sense.text:
When Israel fell to Babylon and Assyria, Edom began to grow and conquer. He intermingled with Japheth, as he did with the Horites, and became the Latins, the Roman kingdom, and then the Europeans. The real Europeans, Japheth, are black.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made”: Solomon saw Genesis with his own eyes.

“The beginning, ending, and midst of the times.” Solomon saw the beginning of time, the ending of days, and the middle. The beginning of the last days was when Christ was born; the middle is the Middle Ages, the Dark Ages; and now we are in the last days of the last days.

Before Christ, the years counted backwards; when Christ was born, time restarted and moved forward, toward the end. If the earth were billions of years old, why is it the year 2026? We count from Christ, not from the dinosaurs.

precepts.why:
“And two of them shall perish, the middle time approaching.” These are Roman emperors, and the two who perished were Didius Julianus and Pertinax. They were in the way, and once they were killed, a black man, Septimius Severus, took the throne of Rome in 193 AD. He had an Arab wife and two sons, one dark and one light like the mother.

“The middle time approaching”: once those two fell, the Middle Ages began, and we ruled over Europe for over a thousand years. Blacks ruled the earth that long, and for the most part we were not righteous, a bunch of evil Negroes with crowns on.

“Four shall be kept until their end begin to approach: but two shall be kept unto the end.” The middle time of Ezra is the same “midst of the times” that Solomon saw.

sense.text: John “saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.” This is Edom. The seven heads are Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain; America is the eighth, which comes out of Britain. The ten horns are the ten common markets, the European Union. These are the European powers, which the writings of our forefathers in the Middle Ages said Edom would become.

“Like unto a leopard”: he took on the attributes of the Greek Empire, democracy, which was born in Athens; and the Senate was born in Rome. “His feet were as the feet of a bear”: he borrowed duality, as the Medes and Persians, Republican and Democrat, to give the people an illusion of choice where there is none. It is an oligarchy: the rich rule behind the scenes, the deep state, the shadow government, the dukes, and the presidents and governors are puppets.

“His mouth as the mouth of a lion”: that is Babylon. Babylonian customs, the new year, the confusion and boldness, the banking system, the IMF and the World Bank, learned from the records of Babylon and Assyria.

“And the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.” The dragon is the devil. That is how Edom rebuilt the desolate places: with the power of Satan. He has authority to tell you who is who and what is what: religion, politics, education, media, social media, the food and medical industries. Most of our thoughts are the television.

“I saw one of his heads as it were wounded to death.” That was Rome, wounded when Septimius Severus took over, as in 2 Esdras 12. It was a wound, but the head did not fall. “And his deadly wound was healed”: in the Renaissance, the Reconquista, the white power structure rose back to power through Spain, Portugal, Britain and the rest, all of which go back to Rome. “And all the world wondered after the beast.”

“And they worshipped the dragon which gave power unto the beast.” The black man worships the white man as God because Satan gave him power: by keeping his New Year, his Christmas, his Thanksgiving, his white Jesus, his Christianity. Even his technology: he can turn a man into a woman with pills, so surely he must be God. That is witchcraft; that is Satan. You think you voted; he voted through you.

This is the Dark Ages, when we as the Moors conquered Edom: we took Spain, Italy, Rome and Britain, subjugated them, and forced them into the caves.

“They that are younger than I have me in derision”: those who are less than us, not chosen, now despise us. “Whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock”: I would not even let my dogs near them. That is how vile they are.
“Yea, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?” They cannot help me, an old man. They are good for nothing to me.

“For want and famine they were solitary”: forced into an isolated place. “Fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.” That is them in the Caucasus Mountains between the Black and Caspian Seas, and in the caves of Covadonga, Asturias, in Spain, where we drove them as the Moors.

The history books say it: the Spanish Goths fled before the march of the Moors into the mountain valleys of Asturias and Galicia, and were killed down to thirty men and ten women, living on honey in the crevices of the rock. The Moors said, What are thirty barbarians perched upon a rock? and let them be, and from those thirty they rose to what they are now. In the cave of Covadonga the purity of their Latin tongue was lost, and the Spanish language was made: Castilian is cave language.

“Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat”: they had to eat off the mountains. The wild man of the medieval European books scratched tubers and roots out of the ground, picked berries, crawled on all fours, ate his game completely raw, and by many accounts was a cannibal; that is where the werewolf comes from.

“They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)” because they were thieves, evil and liars, so we chased them into the mountains, where they had been from the beginning under Mount Seir. “To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.” That is Edom.

“Among the bushes they brayed”: animal noises. That is their history, the Neanderthal, the caveman. Their own books picture the first known German as a Neanderthal, and the wild man of their myths living hairy and naked in the mountains and forests of the German-speaking lands, Austria and Switzerland, with no clothes on, while we were in the castles with crowns and armor.

“They were children of fools, yea, children of base men”: men of no name, no culture, stealing and killing everything, destroying the earth and hunting animals to extinction. That is not our nature. “They were viler than the earth”: the most vile nation on the planet, disgusting and vile. Ask Epstein: hunting girls and hunting babies, trafficking babies, blood on the mattresses and the baby blankets. That is them.

“And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.” Now they mock us: you call yourselves Jews? The land is ours now. They call us kushi, and schwartzer in German. “They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.” We have seen them spit and vomit in our sisters’ faces in public. This is them publicly disrespecting us, these cave dwellers. For them to go from the caves to this, that is God.

“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof.” He covers the faces of the judges: the Messiah, the heavenly Father, the angels, the Israelites, and even our leaders in the Dark Ages.

We ruled over them. The old images of the court of the King’s Bench in the Great Hall at Westminster show black judges and a black king judging matters: that was our hall, and Oxford and Cambridge were ours. James the Second and Seventh, the grandson of King James of the Bible, sits among his counsellors with his guard behind him, and Charles the Seventh was a black man. We were the kings and judges of the earth, and they whitewashed all of it.
“These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it; whereas the Lord was there.”

“I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them.” “And I will make myself known among them, when I have judged thee”: he will make himself known among us.

“I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel.” Revelation 13 said the beast has upon his heads the name of blasphemy. “Saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume”: we are enslaved, given to them to consume, spiritually and literally eaten, physically and literally destroyed.

precepts.why: “The breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” The breath came into us: this is now. While they are distracted by the war with Iran, we are rising up. The word of God is spreading and we are waking up as an exceeding great army. That is how he makes himself known among us when he judges Edom.

Read with the verses before it. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” “Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit”: lies. “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”: his own mother’s son is us, and he says we are not God’s people.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence”: I let you do it. “Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”: they made the heavenly Father white, the angels white, Christ white, and made themselves gods. I am not you. “But I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes”: I will correct you and let you know that I am among them, as Ezekiel says. “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.”

These are the blasphemies Edom has spoken: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” They are the chief house of the devil. The dragon gave him his power, his seat and great authority.

“Them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie”: they say they are Jews, Israelis, and they lie; that is their blasphemy. “Behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee”: they will know who the real Jews are, because it is obviously not them.

The Jewish Encyclopedia shows who they are: King Bulan of the Khazars examined the Muslims, the Christians and the Jews and adopted Judaism. The Khazars, Europeans converted to Judaism, held a tradition that they once dwelt near the mountains of Seir. When the Russians and Byzantines overthrew them, some fled to the Caucasus, and members of their royal family went to Spain and became conquistadors, who came to this side of the world and conquered us here. Edom and the Khazarians are the same people, the Israelis of today.

sense.text: “Come near, ye nations, to hear.” “For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies: he hath utterly destroyed them, he hath delivered them to the slaughter.” This is war. “The mountains shall be melted with their blood.”

“The heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.” That is nuclear destruction, the missiles falling.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea.” Who is in heaven? Edom, the ruling kingdom of today. “And upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” The other versions make it plain: the people I have totally destroyed, the nation marked for destruction, the people devoted to destruction, designated for destruction. That is their purpose: to be destroyed.

“The sword of the Lord is filled with blood”: sacrifice and death, all bloodshed. “For the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah”: Bozrah was a capital of Edom. “And a great slaughter in the land of Idumea”: that is the land of Israel today, the Near East. “Their land shall be soaked with blood.”
“For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.” What is the controversy of Zion? Zechariah answers it.

precepts.why:
“Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?” The same lump is Isaac: one child was made for honour and one for dishonour.

“The vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”: which child of Isaac was the vessel of wrath fitted to destruction? Edom, as Isaiah 34 just said, the people of his curse. “And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory”: we are the vessels of mercy.

So Edom is prepared, predestined for destruction in totality. There is no saving any of them, no matter how good you think they are, however much you love grandma and mama.

The controversy of Zion: “In that day will I make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people: all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces.” Whoever holds Jerusalem will find it a burdensome stone. The Israelis are trying to hold on to that land and expand it as much as they can, but it is becoming a burdensome stone to them, because they are not the chosen people of God and it does not belong to them.

sense.text: “For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city shall be taken, and the houses rifled”: that is the Israelis. “And half of the city shall go forth into captivity”: into the hands of the Palestinians.

“Then shall the Lord go forth, and fight against those nations”: he returns in the time of the war that is taking place over there. “His feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives”: Christ left from the mount of Olives and will land right back in the same place. “And the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof.”

“At evening time it shall be light”: bombs flying, destruction, nukes, light in the darkness. “Living waters shall go out from Jerusalem” after the war takes place. “And the Lord shall be king over all the earth”: that is not right now. “In that day shall there be one Lord, and his name one”: we will all know and speak his true name.

“And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.” It is the land. When the Lord returns, men shall dwell in it and there will be no more war or destruction there.

So if the ones over there now are the rightful people, why is war taking place? Prophecy says the Messiah must return for us to get into the land, not before. Our last and final return is after the Messiah comes, and they themselves say they still wait for the Messiah. That is why they are being blown to hell over there.

precepts.why: “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders.” That is the time when all of Israel is in the land: no bombs in Tel Aviv, Ashdod or Ashkelon. That is not now. “But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise”, because we will be safe living in them.
“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever.” Are the people in Israel today all righteous? No. So they cannot be the ones. It makes no sense at all.

“After many days thou shalt be visited”: by our Lord and Saviour. “In the latter years thou shalt come into the land that is brought back from the sword, and is gathered out of many people”: this is when we are brought back into the land. “Against the mountains of Israel, which have been always waste”: is the land still waste today? Yes, even worse. “But it is brought forth out of the nations, and they shall dwell safely all of them.”

Are the Israelis dwelling safely now? No. They are in bomb shelters, running and hiding. If they are the people, where is their God?

“I will go up to the land of unwalled villages; I will go to them that are at rest, that dwell safely, all of them dwelling without walls, and having neither bars nor gates.” Over there now it is all walls. They are not dwelling safely at all, so they are not the ones.

sense.text: “When I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, I will also gather all nations”, “and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.” Why does he emphasize my people and my land? Because in the last days Christianity would make us think Christ comes to save all people. He says no: I am coming to save my people, and my land for my people.
“And they have cast lots for my people”: they auctioned us off. “And have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine”: men made breeders and girls sold.

“O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine”: in this context the Hamites and the Arabs, whom God did not choose as his people. “Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things”: the Arabs built their temple on top of where Solomon’s temple stood.

“The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” The Hamites and the Arabs sold us to the Grecians, the Greeks and Romans, Edom, the same ones who fled to Spain: the trans-Saharan and the transatlantic slave trade, to remove us far from our border, especially the land of Israel.

“Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head: and I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah”: to have them as slaves. “And they shall sell them to the Sabeans”: the Somalis.

“Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men.” Arise, let us rise up against her in battle. “Let all the men of war draw near”: Iran, Saudi Arabia, China, Russia, do your thing. “Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears: let the weak say, I am strong.” The weak are the Palestinians, the Iranians, all the nations the Europeans have weakened over time, saying, We can defeat America; we can defeat Israel: the same thing.

“Assemble yourselves, and come, all ye heathen”: “thither cause thy mighty ones to come down, O Lord”: the angels, and Christ. “Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about”, as Isaiah 34 and Zechariah 14 said. The valley of Jehoshaphat is the valley of decision in the Near East.

“Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe”, “for their wickedness is great.” It is time for us to go home. “Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision”: the Near East.

“The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining”: destruction coming, nuclear bombs, dark skies and black rain. “The Lord also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem”: he appears in the Near East, on the mount of Olives, “and the heavens and the earth shall shake” when he lands. “But the Lord will be the hope of his people”: not all people, his people, “and the strength of the children of Israel.”
“Then shall Jerusalem be holy, and there shall no strangers pass through her any more.”

“Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land.” No more America, and no more Israelis either. “But Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.”
